questions.stem: Why is bile important for the digestion of lipids?

options.text: Bile chemically breaks down lipids into fatty acids
Bile emulsifies fats into smaller droplets, increasing the surface area for lipase to work on
Bile dissolves lipids so they can be absorbed directly
Bile converts lipids into glucose for energy

questions.explanation: Bile does not chemically digest fats. Instead, it emulsifies them, breaking large fat globules into smaller droplets. This increases the surface area available for lipase enzymes to act on.
